title: E1 — Graph store core — 3 types, one file, fold
description:
The substrate. Everything blocks on this and nothing in it is optional.

**There is one file.** §0.5 deleted the derived snapshot; §0.6 deleted `blobs/`, `plan/` and `schema.json`. Every read folds `mutations.jsonl`.

**Gate:** folding the same log twice yields an identical graph; a torn final line is tolerated.

**TypeScript 7** (native Go port, 2026-07-08). Bun transpiles and runs TS itself, so `tsc` is the **typecheck gate only** — and 8–12x faster there.

- `strict: true` and `module: esnext` are now **defaults** — free
- `types: []` is the new default, so add `"types": ["bun"]` explicitly or Bun globals vanish
- `paths`, never `baseUrl`. No `target: es5`, no `moduleResolution: node`
- ⚠ **No programmatic API until 7.1.** typescript-eslint needs TS 6 side-by-side via `@typescript/typescript6` (ships `tsc6`). Install it if lint uses typed rules
- ⚠ **Unverified:** whether StrykerJS's TS checker works on 7.0. Same class of dependency. Mutation score is a target not a gate (§7), so the downside is bounded — but check before relying on it

Plus project refs, lint, test runner, and a cycle check that fails `bun run build`.

**Done when:** every package builds, no cycles, lint and typecheck clean.

title: T1.2 — packages/core — 2 node types, 1 edge kind, 5 statuses
description:
**2 node types** — `task`, and `wait` with three match kinds (`event` · `human` · `predicate`, the last being what used to be `quorum`). **1 edge kind** — `blocks` with an optional `condition`; §0.8 deleted `supersedes` and `compensates` because both were already node fields, represented twice. **Edge record is `{from, to, condition?}` — no identity.** **5 statuses** (`active|sending|done|failed|dropped`). `status`/`outcome`/`output`, typed deadlines in 3 shapes.

Collapsing `quorum` into `wait` gave it a **mandatory deadline it never had**, closing the liveness hole where a quorum with no clock hangs forever.

Recorded tension: **the store knows two types; the authoring prompt may still say more words.**

**Zero dependencies — this unblocks W3 and W4.**

title: E2 — Mutation engine — 6 ops, 3 invariants, CAS
description:
The code that stands between the LLM and the file. Builds a candidate graph in memory, checks the invariants, and only then touches disk — so a bad batch is never half-applied.

Cut to 6 ops by §0.5, 3 invariants by §0.7; §0.6 cut the taxonomy underneath. T2.6 is never-cut.

spec.md §6.4, §6.7 · 8.5h human / 2.1h AI

title: T2.1 — The 6 ops — apply functions, fixed internal order
description:
add_node · add_edge · set_status · record_outcome · record_output · supersede_node.

Internal order: additions and rewires BEFORE cancellations (Zeebe). A batch violating that order is rejected, never silently reordered.

**§0.5 deleted five ops** — `fan_out`, `add_wait`, `insert_compensation`, `reroute_edge`, `resolve_gate`. All five were `add_node`/`add_edge` with sugar: **the atomic unit is the commit, not the op**, so a batch already gives the all-or-nothing guarantee `fan_out` existed to provide. That also deletes the auto-wiring table (old T2.3), which caused every orphan in the v2 probe.

No `delete_node`. No `rollback` opcode, not even reserved.

---

title: T2.4 — The 3 enforced invariants + parser + CAS check
description:
**A zod parser first, free:** legal type + required fields, legal edge kind, a `condition` on every wait out-edge, and every wait having a deadline + `on_timeout`. Those are *shape*, not graph properties.

**Then three invariants:**
1 terminal & effect protection — an **op-delta** predicate against pre-commit head state
2 predicate-waits stay satisfiable (what `quorum` used to be)
3 **effects are bounded and addressed** — (a) cumulative sends ≤ the approved budget; (b) `recipient_ref` resolves to an evidenced entity. §0.7 merged these: both answer *may this effect exist?* at the same moment. Clause (b) is what stops the mutator inventing people to email

Plus CAS on `parent_v`. **#1 is op-delta, not a post-state scan** — as a state predicate it rejected every commit once any node reached `done`.

Stryker target: 100.

---
**Effort:** 2h / 30m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.4
notes:
PARTIAL after slice 1. DONE: zod parser, invariant 1 (op-delta vs pre-commit head), role authority, CAS.

REMAINING:

INVARIANT 2 (predicate-waits stay satisfiable). Needs NO new types: population is the wait blocking in-edges, and it reads status.outcome.verdict / status.outcome.attrs. `satisfiable iff matching_confirmed + still_live >= n`.
 - status.outcome is now a PROJECTION over an append-only status.outcomes list. Read status.outcome (the first RESOLVING verdict); never outcomes[0], which may be a tentative or a late reply.
 - VERDICTS is 10, not 6: REPLY_VERDICTS + DECISION_VERDICTS (accept|edit|respond|ignore).
 - "still_live" MUST use the same notion of live as T2.6 branch resolution — a dropped source neither satisfies nor blocks. Build T2.6 first, then invariant 2 against it.

INVARIANT 3(b) recipient-evidence — the highest-value check in the codebase, and it needs no new types. At n=60 the mutator met an unsatisfiable predicate by INVENTING counterparties and queueing email to them, passing every other check. A recipient existing only in the proposing batch is rejected.

INVARIANT 3(a) — RESOLVED 2026-08-21, and now LOAD-BEARING. The budget lives on the GENESIS RECORD as config.effect_budget, written by `kona init --config <file>`; read it with pursuitConfig(records) from @kona/core. Chosen over a second file because §6.1 allows .kona/ exactly two files and §6.7 requires reconstructibility from the log alone — a config.json would be unversioned and silently editable after the human approved a plan that depended on it. FAIL CLOSED when it is absent: an unknown cap is not an unlimited one (see checkBudget in packages/core/src/brief.ts for the shape).
 - Why it matters more than it did: max_reattempts has been deleted (it could never fire — one node has one effect slot). The research demand that "without a budget an LLM mutator will retry forever" is now carried ENTIRELY by 3(a). Nothing else bounds a runaway loop.
 - Count spent sends with hasSentEffect() across graph.nodes, as checkBudget does.

REBASE onto main before starting — core has moved: append-only outcomes, derived resolutions, readiness helpers, the outbox ledger, correlation, and pursuit config.

SEAM: packages/core/src/validate.ts only. checkInvariant1 is a standalone exported function so 2 and 3 can be added beside it without touching validate().

comments.author: ivorobiev
comments.text:
Slice 2. Invariant 2 DONE, invariant 3(b) SPLIT and half shipped, 3(a) DEFERRED by Ilya's ruling.

## Invariant 2 — done

`checkInvariant2` + `countPredicate` + `parseCountPredicate` in `validate.ts`. Closed grammar
(`{"count":{"verdict":…,"attrs":…},"op":">=","n":…}`), parsed at validate time and **not**
narrowed in `schema.ts`: `MutationRecordSchema` re-parses every historical line on every fold,
so tightening the committed shape is retroactive — a predicate that no longer parses turns its
record into `UNPARSEABLE_RECORD`, and the expected-version chain then cascades every following
line into `VERSION_DISCONTINUITY`, refusing the log forever.

`still_live` shares one notion of live with T2.6, as required: the exclusion is
`state === "dropped"` and nothing else, in both `countPredicate` and `isReady`.

**It is a transition guard, not a state predicate.** Skip if satisfiable post; skip if already
unsatisfiable at head; skip if the batch legitimately closes the wait. Without the second
carve-out it repeats invariant 1's original bug in a worse form — one broken wait refuses every
later commit forever and the pursuit has no legal move left.

Per Ilya's Q2 ruling it fires only from an actor that can author the repair: not a subagent
(`checkAuthority` forbids all three remedies to one), and not on a mechanically-determined
closure, because `kona resume` has no model to re-plan with.

## Invariant 3(b) — the grammar ships, resolution does not

`MALFORMED_RECIPIENT_REF` and `LITERAL_RECIPIENT_ADDRESS`, both REFUSED/exit 1, deliberately
NOT `UNEVIDENCED_RECIPIENT` — §6.9's human gate keys on that token alone, and "route this to a
human" must never share a token with "the model wrote a bad string".

Every recipient in the repo parses; the n=60 fabrications (`person:club-reserve/goalie-1`,
`roster.bench[0..5]`) do not.

**Resolution is blocked, and the reason is structural**: the folded graph materialises exactly
one `evidence_ref`, `OutcomeRecord`'s. `record_output` parses one and `apply.ts` discards it,
so there is nothing for a ref to resolve *against*. Unblocking it is an `apply.ts` +
`graph.ts` change (retain `record_output`'s evidence), both outside this week's seam.

## Invariant 3(a) — deferred to T3.4, plus a prerequisite nobody had priced

Ilya's Q4 ruling. And the gap is worse than one undefined integer: **`effect_log` has no
writer.** Four sites, all reads — declared `graph.ts:67`, initialised `[]` `apply.ts:88`,
cloned `apply.ts:54`, read `validate.ts:98`. Consequences:
- a reserve-time ledger's `consumed` is structurally ZERO, so send #41 is never refused;
- invariant 1's `UNCOMPENSATED_SUPERSEDE` is unreachable from any real log (its test reaches
  it only by hand-pushing an entry);
- §6.7's "every irreversible node's `effect_log`, derivable from the file alone" is false today.

`kona-e3-3zc.4` needs that prerequisite added: a legal way for `effect reserve`/`record` to
write an `effect_log` entry — a schema+apply change, or the seventh op §6.4 forbids.

## Docs owed

§8 DoD says "All 3 invariants enforced pre-commit"; `README.md:30` likewise. #3 now splits:
3(b) with E2, 3(a) with the outbox.

## Also landed here (not in the original scope)

Two parser-class refusals §6.7 files under "the parser first" that nothing implemented:
- `UNCONDITIONED_WAIT_EDGE` — §6.2's "every out-edge of a wait must carry a condition",
  asserted in three places (`spec.md:172`, `spec.md:282`, `schema.ts:3`) and enforced in none.
  Cannot be a zod rule: `add_edge` carries `from` as an id, never the source's type.
  Branch resolution depends on it — an unconditioned wait out-edge has no resolution to
  compare against, so its arm silently survives its own gate.
- `MISSING_PREDICATE` — a `kind:"predicate"` wait carrying no predicate committed cleanly,
  yielded zero arms, and was therefore treated as satisfiable forever: permanently exempt from
  the invariant that exists to watch it.

## Known limitations, decided rather than missed

- A predicate-wait **created by this batch** is not judged (the guard iterates `pre`). The
  shipped fixture grows `goalie-confirmed`'s population across v2/v5/v7, so judging a wait
  against its empty population at creation would refuse legitimate incremental authoring.
- `still_live` is state-local, so a member that can never *produce* the counted verdict still
  counts as live — e.g. a `{kind:"human"}` wait (`accept|edit|respond|ignore`) counted against
  a predicate wanting `confirmed`, which is the shipped fixture's own shape. The premise break
  fires one commit late there.

title: T2.6 — Branch resolution — store drops untaken branches
description:
**NEVER CUT.** On terminal resolution the store marks untaken branch targets `dropped`, transitively, stopping at any node still held by a live blocking in-edge. An in-edge whose SOURCE is dropped is excluded from merge evaluation.

Readiness fails safe and does NOT inherit the exclusion — otherwise the second node on an untaken branch has no blocker, lands on the frontier, and gets dispatched.

Without this, v2's dominant silent deadlock returns.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.6
notes:
DESIGN DECISION, settle before writing code.

Branch resolution must EXPAND INTO EXPLICIT OPS AT COMMIT TIME. It must NOT run as an implicit cascade inside applyOps().

Why: fold() replays every record through applyOps (packages/core/src/fold.ts:105). A cascade living inside applyOps therefore re-runs on EVERY fold, forever, using whatever the code does TODAY. Change the drop rule in a month and every historical log folds to a different graph than the one the human approved. That breaks D1 (resurrection) and it breaks it silently — the log is unchanged, so nothing looks wrong.

Same principle already settled for id minting: the store decides ONCE, at commit, and the log records the decision. `kona mutate` normalizes the batch (refs resolved, ids minted) and writes the COMMITTED form; fold is a dumb replay that mints nothing and derives nothing. Branch drops belong in exactly that category.

So: when a wait resolves, `mutate` appends the derived `set_status(..., dropped)` ops to the batch it is about to commit, and the rationale explains them. The drops become visible in the log, diffable in the viewer, and stable under code change.

Seam: this is packages/core (a pure function computing the drop set) plus one call site in packages/kona/src/commands/mutate.ts. Coordinate on the mutate.ts line only.

Spec: §6.4 branch resolution. Readiness FAILS SAFE and does not inherit the merge exclusion — a dropped source never satisfies readiness, or the second node on an untaken branch lands on the frontier and gets dispatched, pivot send included.
close_reason: branch.ts + expansion in validate(); zero lines under packages/kona. See comment.

comments.author: ivorobiev
comments.text:
DONE. `packages/core/src/branch.ts` + expansion inside `validate()`.

**Expanded into explicit ops at commit time, as pinned** — and it needed ZERO lines under
`packages/kona/`: `runMutate` already writes `validated.value.ops` into the record, so derived
`set_status(…, "dropped")` ops appended by `validate()` land in the log by themselves.
`fold` never reaches `branch.ts`.

Verified end to end through the CLI: an author's 2-op batch commits as 4, each drop carrying
`derived:branch-resolution:<immediate cause>`, and the untaken arm leaves the frontier.

## What the implementation settles beyond the note

- **`isEdgeDead` is the complement of *pending*, not of `isEdgeSatisfied`.** An edge whose
  source is still open is neither satisfied nor dead. Conflating them drops live branches.
- **Emission is gated; traversal is not.** A node already terminal, `sending`, or carrying an
  `effect_log` is not rewritten — the cascade walks past it. Stopping there arms a pivot: a
  `done` node on an all-dead arm leaves its successors a *satisfied* plain edge, which puts
  them on the frontier and sends the email. `withheld` reports the ones not rewritten.
- **Two seed restrictions, and they are a pair.** Derivation reads only edges that existed at
  head; an edge born dead is refused by the new `DEAD_ON_ARRIVAL_EDGE` instead. Without both,
  the same authored ops give a dropped node when committed together and a permanently
  unreachable one when split in two — the graph becomes a function of the commit boundary.
- **The cascade reaches the merge itself.** A join whose every in-edge originates at a dropped
  node is dropped, not left hanging one hop short.
- **It triggers on any newly-dead edge, not only a resolving wait.** So `supersede_node` now
  cascade-drops the superseded node's exclusive subtree. Broader than §6.4's literal "when a
  wait resolves" sentence; flagged for Ilya rather than assumed.

## Prerequisite that had to land first

§6.4 contradicts itself — :231 says a dropped in-edge "neither satisfies nor blocks", :233 says
readiness "does not inherit the exclusion". Both cannot hold for a node with >1 in-edge, and
the shipped fixture proves it: `goalie-confirmed` had a `satisfied`-conditioned in-edge from
`wait-for-priya`, dropped at v7, and was unreachable FOREVER — before any branch resolution.
Ilya ruled: exclude dropped sources, zero-live ⇒ not ready, honour `merge`. That one function
in `graph.ts` is the only edit outside the seam, and it gave `spec.merge` its first consumer.

Spec follow-up: §6.4:231 "terminal" → "terminal-**success**", so a `failed` in-edge cannot
satisfy a merge.

## Tests

`packages/core/test/branch.test.ts` — 38, incl. §7's branch-drop transitivity and the
"untaken arm, two deep" row (both nodes dropped, neither on the frontier, the merge satisfies
rather than hanging), determinism, and replay-equals-preview.

title: T2.7 — O_EXCL lockfile (portable) + compare-and-swap
description:
**An `O_EXCL` lockfile, not `flock`.** `fs.open(path,'wx')` fails atomically if the file exists, on macOS, Linux and Windows alike; `flock` is POSIX-only and Windows has no equivalent. Same amount of code — write the portable one first.

Store `{pid, started_at}` in the lock and treat one older than the longest legal write as stale.

Then compare-and-swap: `--base-version` must equal head, else **exit 3 + `STALE_BASE_VERSION` + the current head**. Re-read and re-decide, never blind-merge.

*(54 cross-actor overwrites in Beads' data were median 31 minutes apart — the enemy is hand-offs, not races, so the fix is rejection.)*

---
**Effort:** 2h / 30m · **Epic:** E2 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md §1, §6.7 · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T2.7
close_reason: O_EXCL lockfile with {pid, started_at}. Stale reclaim is by RENAME, not unlink-then-create: the latter is not atomic across two reclaimers and both would have believed they held it. CAS is checked INSIDE the lock, since folding before locking validates against a head another writer can move.

spec.md §6.5, §6.6, §6.7.4 · 12.5h human / 3.1h AI

title: T3.1 — Wait schema — or-group conditions, deadline evaluation
description:
First-wins or-group. `deadline` non-nullable, `on_timeout` required. Four-way resolution `satisfied|timeout|bounced|dropped`. `last_checked_at` so the viewer can tell patient from stuck.

**One type, three match kinds** (§0.7): `{kind:"event"}` an inbound reply · `{kind:"human"}` a decision · `{kind:"predicate"}` a condition over its own blocking in-edges — what `quorum` used to be, and it now inherits the mandatory deadline.

Matching is deterministic: plus-tag, then `In-Reply-To`. **A model classifies the reply's *intent*; `kona` never decides whether an event happened.**

Plus the three states retry never converged on: late reply, tentative, quorum-met bulk.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E3 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T3.1
close_reason: Deadline evaluation done: all three shapes, {expr} resolved via its backstop rather than by shipping an expression evaluator §6.8 refused. An uncomputable deadline is NOT expired — fails safe. Wait schema (match kinds, or-group conditions, on_timeout) was already typed in T1.2. Inbound matching is T3.2 and needs the mailbox port.

title: T3.2 — Correlation derivation + inbound matching
description:
`ilya+kona-<node_id>@…` in Kona's own Reply-To. First-match-wins routing, dedupe on provider message-id. Two independent correlation keys: the plus-tag and In-Reply-To.

Reconciliation against a durable cursor is the source of truth; webhooks are a latency optimisation.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E3 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T3.2

title: T3.3 — Outbox — reserve, fsync, send, record
description:
`effect_key = hash(node_id, created_by_version)` — **payload-independent by design**. `payload_hash` computed at reserve. Same key + different payload_hash = loud error, never a second send.

Three crash windows: before fsync (safe), fsync-to-send (safe to retry), **send-to-record (must ask a human)** — the one everybody forgets and every demo hits.

Stryker target: 100.

---
**Effort:** 3h / 45m · **Epic:** E3 · **Spec:** docs/spec.md · **Plan:** docs/plan.md T3.3
notes:
DONE. reserve -> fsync -> send -> record, all three crash windows exercised end to end (spec Q2 was 'the irreversible send has never been exercised').

MECHANISM: no seventh op. reserve/record express themselves via set_status with a structured evidence_ref (effect:reserve:<key>:<payload_hash> / effect:record:<key>:<outcome>:<message_id>), and fold materialises status.effect_log from those transitions. A projection of what the log says, never a decision re-made at read time — same rule as id minting and as branch resolution (T2.6).

effect_key = hash(node_id, created_by_version), payload-independent, 'ek_' + 16 hex.

THREE BUGS FOUND BY RUNNING IT:
 1. payload_hash contains a colon in practice (sha256:abc), and the parser split on its own separator, rejecting the string it had just encoded. effect_log stayed empty -> every duplicate-send guard downstream was unreachable.
 2. hasSentEffect tested for a message_id, but a bounce has one too, so '550 user unknown' read as a successful send.
 3. a completed-but-failed entry satisfied the idempotency check, so a terminal node looked re-reservable.

SPEC CORRECTION for T3.6 (resume): the crash table's rows 2 and 3 are INDISTINGUISHABLE from the log alone — both leave a sending node with completed_at null. 'safe to retry with the same key' and 'must ask a human' describe the same bytes. resume must therefore surface every open reservation for a human (or reconcile against the mailbox, which §6.5 makes truth), never retry one.

NOT DONE: max_reattempts is near-dead. A failed send makes the node terminal, and invariant 1 forbids reopening it, so the retry path is supersede-with-a-replacement — which mints a new node and a new key, with its own counter. The guard is in place and correct but currently unreachable. Flag for Ilya: either accept that retry means a new node, or the spec needs a way back from failed.

title: T2.7a — stale-lock reclaim is not atomic: two writers can both append
description:
Two writers can both hold the lock and both append. Measured: **4 double-wins in 300 runs
(~1.3%)**, and in all four both winners carried `reclaimed: true`. This is the intermittent
failure of `packages/kona/test/lock.test.ts` "exactly one of two concurrent reclaimers wins,
every time" — the test is correct and the code is wrong.

**It also blocks mutation testing entirely.** `bun run mutate:core` aborts in Stryker's dry
run ("There were failed tests in the initial test run") whenever the flake hits, so the §7
floor of 100 on `validate()` cannot be measured on a bad day.

## Root cause — TOCTOU between `readLockInfo` and `rename`

`acquireLock` (packages/kona/src/lock.ts) judges staleness against a holder it read at line
~78, then reclaims by `rename` at line ~99. The rename is atomic, but nothing checks that the
file it moves is still the file that was judged stale.

    A: open(wx) -> EEXIST
    B: open(wx) -> EEXIST
    A: readLockInfo -> {pid 1, T0}   stale
    B: readLockInfo -> {pid 1, T0}   stale        <- both fall through to reclaim
    A: rename(lock, lock.stale-A)    ok
    A: rm(lock.stale-A)
    A: writeLock(lock)               ok           <- A holds a FRESH lock
    B: rename(lock, lock.stale-B)    ok           <- moves A's FRESH lock aside
    B: rm(lock.stale-B)                           <- deletes A's lock
    B: writeLock(lock)               ok           <- B also holds

The comment at the reclaim explains why `rename` beats unlink-then-create, and that reasoning
is right — it just does not cover the case where the loser's `rename` lands *after* the
winner has already published its replacement. The ENOENT window it relies on is only open
between A's rename and A's `writeLock`.

## Fix

After `rename` succeeds, confirm the stashed file is the one judged stale — compare
`started_at` against the `holder` read earlier. If it differs, we just stole a live lock:
rename it back and return `LOCK_HELD`. Restoring is safe because the winner has not written
anything yet under the reclaimed name.

An alternative that removes the window rather than detecting it: reclaim into a
`link()`/`rename()` pair keyed on the stale content hash, so a reclaimer can only ever move a
file whose bytes it has already read.

## Scope note

Found while building T2.6/T2.4 in the `engine` worktree. Not fixed there: `packages/kona/` is
another engineer's seam this week. The repro script and measurement are in that session's
scratchpad and can be turned into a deterministic regression test by injecting a delay between
`rename` and `writeLock`.
close_reason:
FIXED in 57b684a — and by deleting the mechanism rather than repairing it. The analysis in this ticket is exactly right, including the TOCTOU between readLockInfo and rename, and it goes one step further: there is no POSIX compare-and-delete, so the check that judges a lock stale and the removal that takes it cannot be made one operation. Any conditional-reclaim scheme has the same hole somewhere.

So a stale lock is now REPORTED, never reclaimed: reason STALE_LOCK, distinct from LOCK_HELD, with a message naming the holder and telling the operator to make sure no kona process is running and then delete the file — the way git handles index.lock. §6.7 gives write authority to the orchestrator alone, so auto-reclaim was solving a problem this design does not have at the cost of one it would. Reads are unaffected; a stale lock blocks writes only.

A SECOND race in the same file, found while fixing this one: open(path,'wx') is atomic about CREATION but not about content, so for a moment the lock existed EMPTY. A peer reading it in that window saw an unreadable lockfile — the signature of a crash — and would have told the operator to delete a lock somebody was actively holding. The lock is now written to a staging name and link()ed into place: still atomic, still EEXIST on contention, but it never appears without its contents.

The flaky test is replaced by 'two writers can never both hold it', which now holds by construction — 25 rounds of three concurrent acquirers, plus a case asserting that a stale lock produces ZERO winners rather than two.
